rationale:
Evidence: iteration 2 scored 62.76, far below iteration 1 (365.78). The oval went from 17/20 finishes to 0/20, with line_loss_events rising from 0.3 to 2.8. The likely cause is the sensor change: spacing widened from 0.03 m to 0.04 m, and 0.04 m minus the 0.012 m sensor leaves a 0.028 m gap, which is wider than the 0.025 m tape. The tape can then sit entirely between sensors and read as lost. The forward move to y = 0.07 was also untested in isolation. The approved candidate in entityR1 describes the iteration 2 design, which the race has already shown to be worse, so I am not reusing it.

Changes from iteration 1 (the best design): I revert the geometry exactly to iteration 1 (5 sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y = 0.05, sensor_size 0.012). I change one controller variable, base_speed 1.3 to 1.1. In iteration 1 the s-bend and slalom ended just over the 0.06 m limit (max_error 0.0613 and 0.063), and speed was the strongest lever in iterations 0 and 1. kp 1.6, kd 0.5, ki 0 and line_loss last_direction stay the same.

Expected result: max_error on the s-bend and slalom falls below 0.06 m, so more runs finish those tracks. Oval completion time should rise from about 1.92 s to about 2.3 s, which is still under 3.0 s. Line-loss events should stay near iteration 1 levels (about 0.3 on the oval).

Hypotheses to test: (1) speed drives bend error, so 1.1 keeps the robot on the tape through the s-bend and slalom; (2) the iteration 2 failure came from sensor spacing, not speed. Measurements wanted next: per-track completion, progress, max_error, line_loss_events and completion_time. If the s-bend and slalom still exceed 0.06 m, try base_speed 1.0. If the oval fails to finish under 3.0 s, go back to 1.2. If slalom line losses stay above 0.2, test line_loss at search_left or search_right.
